examples.solution_text:
Histogram $H$ is approximately symmetrical and bell-shaped, with most values near the centre. It could represent approximately normally distributed data.

Histogram $J$ is symmetrical, but has fewer values near the centre and two peaks. Symmetry alone is insufficient.

examples.question_text: $A$ and $B$ are normally distributed. Both have mean $60$, but their standard deviations are $3$ and $6$, respectively. Sketch and label their normal curves on the same axes.
$C$ and $D$ are normally distributed with means $24$ and $36$, respectively. Both have standard deviation $4$. Sketch and label their normal curves on the same axes.

examples.solution_text:
(a) Curve $L$: its peak is furthest right.

(b) Curve $M$: its peak is furthest left.

(c) Curve $K$: it is the widest and lowest curve, so its values have the greatest spread.

(d) Curve $M$: it is the narrowest and tallest curve, so its values have the smallest spread.

examples.question_text:
$X$ is normally distributed with mean $48$ and standard deviation $5$.
(a) Find $P(X>48)$.
(b) The area between $43$ and $48$ is approximately $0.34$. Use symmetry to find the approximate probability $P(X>53)$.

examples.derivation: H has symmetric frequencies 2, 4, 7, 9, 7, 4, 2 and one central peak. J has symmetric frequencies 9, 7, 4, 2, 4, 7, 9 but a central trough. Only H has the approximate bell shape required by the source.

Both plotted curves peak at coordinate 0, labelled 60. Their coordinate standard deviations are 1 and 2, matching the required ratio 3:6. Their peak heights are 2 and 1, giving equal total areas and the stated wider, lower curve B.

The axis labels increase by 4 per coordinate unit. Peaks at -1.5 and 1.5 therefore represent 24 and 36. Both curves have coordinate standard deviation 1 and peak height 2, matching standard deviation 4 and a horizontal separation of 12.

K, L and M peak at coordinates 0, 3 and -3, with coordinate standard deviations 2, 1 and 0.5 respectively. Thus L has the largest mean, M the smallest mean, K the largest standard deviation and M the smallest standard deviation. Heights 1, 2 and 4 preserve equal total areas.

Symmetry and total area 1 give P(X>48)=0.5. The scores 43 and 53 are each 5 units from the mean, so the supplied area 0.34 is reflected from the left central interval to the right. Consequently P(X>53) is approximately 0.5-0.34=0.16. The diagram labels these intervals and shades the correct right tail.
